categories.main_business_segments: Genky DrugStores operates primarily as a holding company overseeing a group engaged in the retail of pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, daily goods, and food products through its subsidiary Genky Co., Ltd. The group operates a single business segment focused on drugstore retail, with an emphasis on offering a wide range of daily necessities, including fresh foods, at low prices.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company's core operational methods include standardized 300-tsubo (approx. 990 m2) store formats (R stores), dominant area store clustering, and low-cost operations supported by proprietary logistics centers and process centers for fresh food handling. The group also develops and manages private brand (PB) products and utilizes efficient inventory and store management systems.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Genky DrugStores targets local consumers seeking affordable daily necessities, including families, seniors, and health-conscious individuals. Its main markets are regional communities in central Japan, focusing on areas with limited competition and high demand for cost-effective, one-stop shopping for pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, groceries, and fresh foods.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates 480 stores as of June 2025, concentrated in the Chubu region of Japan, specifically in Aichi, Gifu, Fukui, Ishikawa, and Shiga prefectures. All operations and assets are located within Japan, with no overseas sales or significant international presence.
categories.supply_chain_position: Genky DrugStores is positioned at the downstream end of the supply chain as a retailer, directly serving end consumers. It also manages some upstream activities through its subsidiary Genky Foods, which manufactures food products, and operates its own logistics and process centers for distribution and fresh food processing.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company's strategic focus is on expanding its dominant area presence through standardized store openings, strengthening its private brand product lineup, and enhancing low-cost operations. While there is no formal R&D activity, innovation is pursued in store format standardization, supply chain efficiency, and fresh food assortment. The group emphasizes financial soundness, compliance, and human resource development as key priorities.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated primarily through direct sales of products at company-operated retail stores. The group also earns income from private brand product sales and operates a customer loyalty point system. As a holding company, Genky DrugStores receives management fees and interest from subsidiaries.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other Japanese drugstore chains such as Welcia, Tsuruha, and Matsumotokiyoshi, as well as supermarkets and convenience stores. Genky DrugStores differentiates itself by focusing on low prices, a broad assortment including fresh foods, and dominant regional coverage, positioning itself as a leading discount drugstore in its core markets.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending June 2025, consolidated net sales reached 200.8 billion yen, with operating profit of 9.7 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders of 7.1 billion yen. The company has demonstrated steady growth, with sales increasing by 8.6% year-on-year and consistent store expansion. Total assets stand at 127.3 billion yen, and the group employs 1,841 regular staff and 2,453 part-time/temporary workers.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Genky DrugStores' value proposition centers on being a 'neighborhood store where living costs can be saved,' offering overwhelming low prices and a comprehensive selection of daily necessities, including fresh foods. Its standardized store format, dominant area strategy, and efficient logistics enable it to provide convenience and affordability, differentiating it from both traditional drugstores and supermarkets.
